items.title: Two Nirvāṇas: Liberation Still Wearing a Body, and Liberation Wearing None

items.zh: 如是於現法中諸行不轉；由不轉故，於現法中，於有餘依界證得現法涅槃。彼於爾時，唯餘清淨識緣名色，名色緣識；乃至有識身在，恒受離繫受，非有繫受。此有識身乃至先業所引壽量恒相續住。若壽量盡，便捨識所持身。此命根後所有命根無餘永滅，更不重熟。
items.en: Thus, within the present existence, these formations no longer operate; and because they no longer operate, one realises, within the present existence, nirvāṇa already attained in this very life, within the nirvāṇa-realm with residue remaining. At that time there remains only a purified consciousness conditioning name-and-form, and name-and-form conditioning consciousness; and for as long as this embodied consciousness endures, one constantly experiences only feeling released from bondage, never feeling still bound. This embodied consciousness continues on for exactly as long as the lifespan drawn by past karma lasts. Once that lifespan is exhausted, the body sustained by consciousness is relinquished, and this life-faculty, once ended, ceases entirely without remainder, never to ripen again.

items.zh: 又復此識與一切受任運滅故，所餘因緣先已滅故，不復相續，永滅無餘，是名無餘依涅槃界，究竟寂靜處。亦名趣求涅槃者，於世尊所梵行已立，究竟涅槃。
items.en: And further, once this consciousness and every feeling cease of their own accord, and since every other supporting cause has already ceased as well, nothing continues on — a final cessation without remainder. This is called the nirvāṇa-realm without residue remaining, the place of ultimate tranquility. One who has reached it is also called one who has attained the goal of nirvāṇa: the holy life has been established under the Blessed One, and nirvāṇa is now complete.

items.title: Dependent Origination's Essence, Fully Established — the First of Nine Gateways Closes

items.zh: 如是已說由三種相建立緣起，謂從前際，中際生；從中際，後際生；又於中際，若流轉，若清淨；是名緣起體性。
items.en: Thus it has been explained that dependent origination is established through three aspects: the present arising from the past; the future arising from the present; and, within the present itself, either continuing in transmigration or turning towards purification. This is called the essence of dependent origination.

items.title: Eight Gateways Where Dependent Origination Operates, from a Single Thought to a Whole World-System

items.zh: 緣起門云何？謂依八門，緣起流轉。一、內識生門，二、外稼成熟門，三、有情世間死生門，四、器世間成壞門，五、食任持門，六、自所作業增上勢力受用隨業所得愛非愛果門，七、威勢門，八、清淨門。
items.en: What is the gateway of dependent origination? Dependent origination flows through eight gateways. First, the gateway of an inward consciousness arising; second, the gateway of an outward crop ripening; third, the gateway of a sentient being's death and birth; fourth, the gateway of a physical world's formation and destruction; fifth, the gateway of the four foods sustaining life; sixth, the gateway of one's own accumulated karma's dominant power determining what desirable or undesirable result is experienced; seventh, the gateway of mastery; eighth, the gateway of purification.

items.title: Eight Layers of "Dependent Origination's Meaning" — Answering Every Rival School at Once

items.zh: 緣起義云何？謂離有情義，是緣起義；於離有情復無常義，是緣起義；於無常復暫住義，是緣起義；於暫住復依他義，是緣起義；於依他離作用義，是緣起義；於離作用復因果相續不斷義，是緣起義；於因果相續不斷復因果相似轉義，是緣起義；於因果相似轉復自業所作義，是緣起義。
items.en: What is the meaning of dependent origination? The meaning of being free of any controlling being is the meaning of dependent origination. Free of any such being, and further impermanent — this too is the meaning of dependent origination. Impermanent, and further briefly persisting — this too is the meaning of dependent origination. Briefly persisting, and further dependent on other conditions — this too is the meaning of dependent origination. Dependent on other conditions, yet devoid of any real agency within them — this too is the meaning of dependent origination. Devoid of real agency, and yet cause and result continue unbroken — this too is the meaning of dependent origination. Continuing unbroken, and further with cause and result corresponding to each other — this too is the meaning of dependent origination. Corresponding to each other, and further each being the product of one's own karma alone — this too is the meaning of dependent origination.

items.zh: 問：為顯何義建立緣起耶？答：為顯因緣所攝染污、清淨義故。
items.en: Question: To reveal what purpose is dependent origination established? Answer: To reveal the defiled and the purified meanings both contained within causes and conditions.

items.zh: 緣起差別云何？謂於前際無知等，如經廣說。

items.title: Nineteen Faces of Ignorance, the First Link Anatomized in Full

items.zh: 於前際無知云何？謂於過去諸行起不如理分別，謂我於過去為曾有耶？為曾無耶？曾何體性？曾何種類？所有無知。於後際無知云何？謂於未來諸行起不如理分別，謂我於未來為當有耶？為當無耶？當何體性？當何種類？所有無知。於前後際無知云何？謂於內起不如理猶豫，謂何等是我？我為何等？今此有情從何所來？於此沒已當往何所？所有無知。
items.en: What is ignorance regarding the past? Unsound reflection on past formations — was I, or was I not; what nature did I have; what kind of being was I — all this not-knowing. What is ignorance regarding the future? The same unsound reflection turned towards what is yet to come. What is ignorance regarding the juncture of past and future, the present? Inward, unsound uncertainty — what is this "I"; what is "I" itself; where has this being come from, and where will it go once it perishes here — all this not-knowing.

items.zh: 於內無知云何？謂於各別諸行起不如理作意，謂之為我所有無知。於外無知云何？謂於外非有情數諸行起不如理作意，謂為我所所有無知。於內外無知云何？謂於他相續諸行起不如理分別，謂怨親中所有無知。於業無知云何？謂於諸業起不如理分別，謂有作者所有無知。於異熟無知云何？謂於異熟果所攝諸行，起不如理分別，謂有受者所有無知。於業異熟無知云何？謂於業及果起不如理分別所有無知。
items.en: Ignorance regarding what is inward mistakes one's own aggregates for "I." Ignorance regarding what is outward mistakes non-sentient things for "mine." Ignorance regarding both mistakes another's aggregates as enemy or friend. Ignorance regarding karma mistakes there to be an agent who acts. Ignorance regarding ripened result mistakes there to be a recipient who experiences it. Ignorance regarding karma-and-result together is unsound discrimination about karma and its result.

items.zh: 於佛無知云何？謂於佛菩提，或不思惟、或邪思惟、或由放逸、或由疑惑、或由毀謗所有無知。於法無知云何？謂於正法善說性，或不思惟、或邪思惟、或由放逸、或由疑惑、或由毀謗所有無知。於僧無知云何？謂於僧正行，或不思惟、或邪思惟、或由放逸、或由疑惑、或由毀謗所有無知。於苦無知云何？謂於苦是苦性，或不思惟、或邪思惟、或由放逸、或由疑惑、或由毀謗所有無知。如於苦，當知於集、滅、道無知亦爾。
items.en: Ignorance regarding the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha — towards the Buddha's own awakening, the well-taught nature of the true Dharma, and the Saṅgha's genuine conduct — arises through simply not reflecting, through wrongful reflection, through heedlessness, through doubt, or through outright disparagement. Ignorance regarding suffering is this same failure applied to suffering's own nature as suffering; and, exactly as with suffering, so too with origin, cessation, and the path.

items.zh: 於因無知云何？謂起不如理分別，或計無因、或計自在、世性、士夫、中間等不平等因所有無知。如於因無知，於從因所生諸行亦爾。又彼無罪故名善，有罪故名不善；有利益故名應修習，無利益故名不應修習；黑故名有罪，白故名無罪，雜故名有分。於六觸處如實通達無知云何？謂增上慢者，於所證中顛倒思惟所有無知。如是略說十九種無知。
items.en: Ignorance regarding cause is unsound reflection that posits either no cause at all, or an unequal cause — a sovereign lord, primal nature, a cosmic person, or an intermediate creator; and exactly the same ignorance applies to the formations arising from that cause. These, too, are called wholesome when blameless and unwholesome when blameworthy; worth cultivating when beneficial and not worth cultivating when not; dark when blameworthy, bright when blameless, and mixed when both are intermingled. Ignorance regarding true realisation of the six fields of contact is the distorted thinking of one who, overestimating their own attainment, mistakes what has not truly been realised for what has. These, briefly stated, are the nineteen kinds of ignorance.

blocks.text: Today completes the essence of dependent origination with the two kinds of nirvāṇa, then gives two more of the nine headings: the gateways through which dependent origination operates, and what "dependent origination" means. It ends with the beginning of a detailed analysis of each link, starting with ignorance.

One who has realised liberation still has a body: this is **nirvāṇa with remainder** (有餘依涅槃), with four kinds of peace. Master Cháng Bǎi quotes the *Stage of Nirvāṇa with Remainder*: like a palm tree whose root and crown are cut, it never grows again; all future suffering is cut off. When that body ends, it is **nirvāṇa without remainder** (無餘依涅槃). These are the sixteenth and seventeenth of the seventeen stages (Introduction 2).

Dependent origination operates in eight domains: an inner consciousness arising; an outer crop ripening; beings' death and birth; the world's formation and destruction; **food sustaining life** (Master Cháng Bǎi: the four foods of Day 32); one's karma bearing its results; mastery (as of meditative powers); and purification. It is not only the twelve links of one being's life; it is the pattern of every arising.

What does "dependent origination" mean? The treatise answers in eight layers, each correcting a rival view. The first: dependent origination is "free of any controlling being". Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Yujia lunji*: this refutes the Vaiśeṣikas and, within Buddhism, the Vātsīputrīyas (Day 41), who posit a self as agent. Conditions themselves have no agency, yet cause and result continue.

Venerable Miào Jìng links this to Madhyamaka, quoting Nāgārjuna: "Things arise neither from themselves nor from others, nor from both, nor without cause; hence they are called unarisen." If nothing truly arises, how does dependent origination work? As process, not as things producing things.

Why is dependent origination taught at all? "To reveal the defiled and the purified meanings both contained within causes and conditions." The forward sequence shows how suffering arises; the reverse, how it ends.

Ignorance, the first link, is analysed as nineteen kinds of not knowing: not knowing the past, the future, the present (Venerable Miào Jìng: "prior and posterior" means the present, prior to the future and posterior to the past), the inner, the outer, karma, results, karma-and-result together (the *Pīxún jì*: denying both, as annihilationists do), the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, the four truths, cause and what arises from causes, and others.

"Not knowing cause" includes positing no cause, or an "unequal cause" such as a sovereign lord, primal nature, or a cosmic person: the doctrines of fascicles 6 and 7 appear here as forms of ignorance.

The last is the ignorance of the **overestimator** (增上慢), who thinks he has attained what he has not. Venerable Miào Jìng: when such a person says "I am a Buddha", it is not a lie; "he's sincere; he says what he thinks." That is exactly why it is so dangerous, and why he advises reading the scriptures often: they are a mirror.

quiz.q: One in nirvāṇa with residue has four kinds of peace. Citing the Stage with Residue, what simile does Master Cháng Bǎi give for the peace of suffering?
options: like a palm tree with its root and crown cut off, never to grow again — all future suffering is cut off
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "With all outflows ended, every future suffering is cut off forever … like a palm tree with root and crown severed, never appearing again." Venerable Miào Jìng: this nirvāṇa has four peaces and four virtues. In nirvāṇa without residue, the life-faculty "never ripens again," like a sprout that won't regrow.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, through what eight gateways does dependent origination flow?
options: inward consciousness, outward crops, beings' death and birth, the world's formation and destruction, food, one's karma's results, mastery, purification
quiz.why: "First, the gateway of an inward consciousness arising; second, the gateway of an outward crop ripening; third, the gateway of a sentient being's death and birth; fourth, the gateway of a physical world's formation and destruction; fifth … food; sixth … one's own karma's results; seventh, mastery; eighth, purification." Venerable Miào Jìng: like a great house with eight doors.

quiz.q: The first layer of meaning is "free of any controlling being." Citing the Yuqie lunji, whom does Master Cháng Bǎi say this refutes?
options: the Vaiśeṣikas outside and the Vātsīputrīyas within Buddhism, who hold a self as agent
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "This refutes the non-Buddhist Vaiśeṣikas and, within Buddhism, the Vātsīputrīyas and others who hold a self to be the agent." No one controls dependent origination; acting is just volition, and there's no permanent experiencer.

quiz.q: The text says conditions lack real agency, yet cause and result continue. Which verse does Venerable Miào Jìng cite?
options: "abide nowhere and give rise to mind"
"Things arise neither from self nor other, nor both, nor without cause — hence they are called unarisen"
"all conditioned things are like a dream"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Things arise neither from themselves nor from others, nor both, nor without cause — hence 'unarisen.' If nothing arises, how do things arise? Just like this." No agency, yet cause and result continue unbroken.

quiz.q: The text asks: to reveal what purpose is dependent origination established? What is the answer?
options: to reveal the defiled and purified meanings contained in causes and conditions
quiz.why: "To reveal the defiled and the purified meanings both contained within causes and conditions." The forward sequence shows defilement, the reverse purification, matching the essence's "continuing in transmigration or turning towards purification." Master Cháng Bǎi: continuity means cause ceases and result arises moment by moment.

quiz.q: In "ignorance regarding cause," what unequal causes does the text say are posited?
options: no cause at all, or a sovereign lord, primal nature, cosmic person, or intermediate creator
quiz.why: "Unsound reflection that posits either no cause at all, or an unequal cause — a sovereign lord, primal nature, a cosmic person, or an intermediate creator." Master Cháng Bǎi: misjudging the origin of beings and worlds — either uncaused, or made by some ruler.

quiz.q: The last of the nineteen is the ignorance of the overestimator. When such a person says "I am a buddha," is it a lie, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: no — he's sincere, saying what he truly believes
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: overestimation "isn't lying — he's sincere; he says what he thinks." Hence read the scriptures often: they're a bright mirror showing one's spots. Master Cháng Bǎi: claiming to have attained what one hasn't.
